title: «El ritual de los Musgrave», The Strand Magazine, mayo de 1893

parts.text: Aventuras de Sherlock Holmes XVIII\. — El ritual de los Musgrave {{#anomalia e:holmes q:anomalia|Una anomalía que a menudo me llamaba la atención en el carácter de mi amigo [[holmes|Sherlock Holmes]] era que, aunque en sus métodos de pensamiento fuera el más pulcro y metódico de los hombres}}, en sus costumbres personales era uno de los más desordenados que hayan llevado nunca a la desesperación a un compañero de alojamiento. Pero cuando encuentro a un hombre {{#carbonero e:holmes q:carbonero|que guarda los cigarros en el balde del carbón, el tabaco en la punta de una babucha persa y la correspondencia sin contestar clavada con una navaja en mitad de la repisa de la chimenea}}, empiezo a darme aires de virtud. {{#destruir e:holmes q:destruir|Le horrorizaba destruir documentos, sobre todo los que tenían que ver con sus casos pasados.}} {{#hojalata e:holmes q:hojalata|Se fue a su dormitorio, del que volvió al poco arrastrando tras de sí una gran caja de hojalata.}} {{#casos e:holmes q:casos|—Aquí hay casos de sobra, Watson —dijo, mirándome con ojos traviesos—.}} Creo que si supiera usted todo lo que tengo en esta caja, me pediría que sacara algunos en vez de meter otros.

src_en.anomalia: An anomaly which often struck me in the character of my friend Sherlock Holmes was that, although in his methods of thought he was the neatest and most methodical of mankind
src_en.carbonero: who keeps his cigars in the coal-scuttle, his tobacco in the toe end of a Persian slipper, and his unanswered correspondence transfixed by a jack-knife into the very centre of his wooden mantelpiece
src_en.destruir: He had a horror of destroying documents, especially those which were connected with his past cases
src_en.hojalata: he went off to his bedroom, from which he returned presently pulling a large tin box behind him.
src_en.casos: There are cases enough here, Watson,” said he, looking at me with mischievous eyes.
src_en.papel: I must see that paper, Musgrave,’ said I, ‘which this butler of yours thought it worth his while to consult, even at the risk of the loss of his place.
src_en.catecismo: He handed me the very paper which I have here, Watson, and this is the strange catechism to which each Musgrave had to submit when he came to man’s estate.
src_en.pasos: North by ten and by ten, east by five and by five, south by two and by two, west by one and by one, and so under.
src_en.siglo: The original has no date, but is in the spelling of the middle of the seventeenth century,’ remarked Musgrave.
